teaching_language: Fully English. This is a SINGLE-LANGUAGE programme, not one of unibz's trilingual degrees: the admission document states flatly 'The official teaching language is English' and the brochure 'At a glance' box says 'Courses will be taught in English'. Every course in the published study plan (Software Design and Implementation, Agile Software Development, Human Computer Interaction, Verification and Reliability, Advances in SE and Communication, Cloud Computing and Distributed Systems, Intelligent Tools for Software Evolution, Research Methods, Software and Systems Security, the catalogue alternatives, Internship and Thesis) is delivered in English. There is NO Italian or German course requirement in the current curriculum and no compulsory 'Italian/German for Computer Scientists' course of the kind that exists in the trilingual Bachelor in Computer Science. Historical nuance: students enrolled in 2021/22 had to attend A1.1 German AND Italian courses, and the 2022/23 cohort had to prove A1 CEFR in German and/or Italian or attend Language Centre courses; from the 2023/24 cohort onward no such obligation exists. Italian/German remain available free of charge at the Language Centre as an option, not a requirement.
campus: NOI Techpark Bozen-Bolzano (the university's technology-park campus, Bruno-Buozzi-Straße 1 / via Bruno Buozzi 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano), Faculty of Engineering. This is the same campus as the Bachelor in Computer Science and the Master in Computing for Data Science, physically separate from the main Universitätsplatz/piazza Università campus in the city centre where the Advisory Service sits.
degree_class: LM-18 (Informatica / Computer Science — the Italian master class for computing). 120 ECTS over 2 years. Structure: 60 ECTS mandatory courses + 24 ECTS optional and free-choice courses + 36 ECTS internship and thesis. Graduates may sit the Italian State Examination for admission to the profession of 'Ingegnere dell'informazione' and register in Section A of the Italian Register of Engineers.
offered_in_2026_27: Yes — actively offered and running. The official programme page for 2026/27 carries the status line 'Courses will definetely be starting'. Confirmed empirically: both the Early Bird and the Late ranking lists for a.y. 2026/27 have been published and signed (21/05/2026 and 23/07/2026), students have been admitted in both, and the programme is additionally listed as 'Application possible' in the Additional Application Session (18/08 - 04/09/2026). Classes start 28/09/2026.
is_new_programme: No — not a new programme, but a RENAMED and restructured one. It is the continuation of the former 'Master in Software Engineering for Information Systems'; the unibz study guide states that students enrolled before 2023/24 are enrolled in that previous programme. The name 'Master in Software Engineering' applies from the 2023/24 intake. The curriculum was then substantially revised again for the current intake around the 'AI revolution' theme — the brochure publishes TWO distinct study plans side by side, the current one and a legacy 'Study Plan - enroled form 2024'. So a candidate researching this programme will find older material (and older course names such as Contemporary Software Development, Software Maintenance and Evolution, Parallel Computing, Large Language Models and Information Retrieval) that no longer matches the current first-year plan.
majors_tracks_study_plans: No formal majors or tracks — a single study plan, with specialisation delivered through electives. Current plan: Year 1 Sem 1 — Software Design and Implementation 12 CP (M1 Requirements Engineering for Dependable Systems 6 CP, M2 Software Architecture 6 CP), Agile Software Development 12 CP (M1 Agile Processes and Practices 6 CP, M2 Continuous Integration and Delivery 6 CP), Human Computer Interaction 6 CP. Year 1 Sem 2 — Verification and Reliability 6 CP, Advances in SE and Communication 6 CP, Cloud Computing and Distributed Systems 6 CP, Intelligent Tools for Software Evolution 6 CP, Free Choice 6 CP. Year 2 Sem 3 — Research Methods 6 CP, Software and Systems Security 6 CP, Internship 6 CP, plus 12 CP 'Alternatives from Catalogue' (up to two of: Software Quality and Metrics, Entrepreneurial Software Engineering, Innovative Solutions for Computing Education, Responsible Software Engineering, Prototyping Interactive Application, Algorithms for Parallel Computing). Year 2 Sem 4 — Free Choice 6 CP + Thesis 24 CP. Free Choice credits may be advanced or postponed and may be either lectures or internships, guided by a tutor; catalogue courses may be graded or pass/fail; thesis work may begin from year 2. A separate legacy plan ('enroled form 2024') applies to earlier cohorts, with a 30 CP thesis and different first-year courses. Part-time enrolment is available. An optional internship of maximum 300 hours is offered through the faculty's employer network, alongside exchange programmes with partner universities worldwide.
english_only_accessibility: OPEN — this is one of the genuinely English-accessible unibz programmes and the single most important contrast with the trilingual bachelors. The ONLY language requirement is English at B2; there is no Italian or German requirement at entry, none during the programme, and none to graduate. A candidate who speaks only English faces no language barrier whatsoever. This is decisive when compared with, for example, the Bachelor in Computer Science, where B2 in TWO of three teaching languages is eliminatory and where every single non-EU applicant in the 2026/27 Early Bird session was excluded on language grounds. Here the language filter is minimal: in the entire 2026/27 Late session only ONE applicant was excluded for failing the language requirement. The real constraint for this programme is not language but (a) the curricular ECTS prerequisites in computer science and mathematics and (b) for non-EU applicants, severe competition for the 30 places.
admission_type: Restricted access (numero programmato) with a merit-based ranking list, decided by documentary evaluation of the applicant's study career — NOT by a written entrance exam. There is no TOLC, no CENT-S, no SAT, no aptitude test and no portfolio. Selection is a points-based assessment (maximum 20 points) of degree grade average, the Webometrics ranking of the awarding university, curricular ECTS in computer science/mathematics, and an optional CV. A CONDITIONAL interview mechanism exists as a secondary gate: applicants below the 24/30 grade-average threshold are routed first to a curriculum vitae evaluation and, if that is unsatisfactory, to an online interview in English. Separate ranking lists are drawn up for (a) EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment and (b) non-EU citizens living abroad. English B2 is an eliminatory prerequisite that scores zero points.
academic_requirements: One of two routes. ROUTE A — a bachelor degree in Computer Science (class L-31) or Information Engineering (class L-08), or an equivalent qualification under previous Italian regulations, or an equivalent qualification obtained abroad; the admission document names as examples Computer Science, Software Engineering, Business Informatics and Information Engineering. ROUTE B — a bachelor's degree in ANY discipline together with curricular requirements obtained through bachelor's degrees, master's degrees or single subject courses: at least 12 ECTS in INFO-01/A (ex INF/01) Computer Science or IINF-05/A (ex ING-INF/05) Information Engineering; at least 6 ECTS in MATH-01/A (ex MAT/01) Mathematical Logic, MATH-03/A (ex MAT/05) Mathematical Analysis or MATH-05/A (ex MAT/08) Numerical Analysis; and at least a further 12 ECTS in the sectors above — 30 ECTS in total. The document gives both the post-2024-reform SSD codes and their legacy equivalents. For candidates with a qualification obtained abroad, 'the verification of the curricular requirements is based on the specific contents of the educational activities' — i.e. course content, not the degree title, decides, which is what makes Route B workable for non-Italian degrees. GRADE THRESHOLD: candidates must have an average mark of at least 24/30; those below it are not automatically rejected but must pass a CV evaluation and, failing that, an online interview. At enrolment a foreign degree must be shown to carry at least 180 ECTS and to give access to a master programme. National rule: simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 programmes is allowed, provided they are not in the same class (e.g. not LM-18/LM-18) and differ in at least 2/3 of course contents. unibz provides an 'unofficial assessment tool' on the programme page for self-checking eligibility.
entry_exam_or_test: NO written entrance examination of any kind — no unibz aptitude test, no TOLC-I, no CENT-S, no SAT, no GRE/GMAT. Admission is decided on documents. The only examination-type events connected to admission are: (1) an ONLINE INTERVIEW IN ENGLISH, but only as a fallback for candidates below the 24/30 average whose CV evaluation was unsatisfactory (dates: Early Bird 21 - 22/05/2026; Late 28 - 29/07/2026; Additional Session 17/09/2026); and (2) unibz Language Centre English exams, only for applicants who choose that route to prove B2 — Early Bird 16/03/2026 (registration 02 - 09/03/2026) and 16 - 17 and 20 - 21/04/2026 (registration 24/03 - 08/04/2026); Late 22 - 26/06/2026 (registration 28/05 - 15/06/2026). Note that NO unibz language exam session is offered for the Additional Application Session, so applicants in that window must hold an external certificate (e.g. LanguageCert, TOEFL, IELTS). A non-selective Mathematics pre-course runs 21/09 - 09/10/2026 for enrolled students; it is preparatory, not an admission test.
selection_scoring: Points-based ranking, MAXIMUM 20 POINTS, composed of four elements: (1) the admission title scored UP TO 10 POINTS based on the grade average obtained at the time of application; (2) UP TO 3 POINTS weighting the study curriculum by the Webometrics Ranking of World Universities (see bonus_points); (3) UP TO 3 POINTS for curricular ECTS in computer science (INF/01, ING-INF/05) and/or mathematics (MAT/01, MAT/05, MAT/08) — 3 points for more than 120 ECTS, 2 points for 81-120 ECTS, 1 point for 41-80 ECTS, 0 points for less than 40 ECTS; (4) the Curriculum Vitae scored UP TO 4 POINTS based on the relevance of the listed experiences. The English B2 certificate 'does not give a score but is an admission prerequisite'. MINIMUM GRADE AVERAGE: 24/30. Candidates below it must pass a CV evaluation of work experience in Software Engineering, Computer Engineering and Applied Computer Science; if that is unsatisfactory they must pass an online interview in English demonstrating knowledge of programming concepts and software engineering. No minimum total-score threshold is published — the ranking is simply ordered by points. COMPETITION LEVEL 2026/27 is sharply asymmetric: for EU applicants the programme was UNDERSUBSCRIBED (9 admitted against 20 Early Bird places; 3 admitted in the Late session), whereas for non-EU applicants living abroad it was heavily OVERSUBSCRIBED — all 30 places filled and a waiting list running to rank 65, i.e. at least 65 ranked non-EU candidates competing for 30 places, roughly 2.2 ranked applicants per place before counting those excluded outright.
bonus_points: The distinctive feature of this programme's scoring is the WEBOMETRICS UNIVERSITY-RANKING BONUS, which rewards the prestige of the institution that awarded the bachelor degree: 3 points for universities in position 1 to 1000 in the Webometrics Ranking of World Universities; 2 points for positions 1001 to 2000; 1 point for positions 2001 to 3000; 0 points for positions 3001 onwards. This is worth up to 15% of the maximum 20-point score and is applied to the candidate's home university, not to the candidate. The same mechanism is used by the Master in Computing for Data Science. A second, effectively bonus-like element is the CURRICULUM VITAE, worth up to 4 points for the relevance of listed experiences — optional to submit, so an applicant who omits it simply forfeits up to 4 points. A third is the curricular-ECTS scale (up to 3 points), which rewards depth of prior computing/mathematics study beyond the bare 30-ECTS minimum. There is NO GMAT/GRE bonus (that belongs to the Master in Accounting and Finance), no startup-project bonus (Entrepreneurship), and no extracurricular-activities bonus of the kind used in the Bachelor in Computer Science.
portfolio_and_materials: No portfolio, no motivation letter, no video, no project proposal and no reference letters are required or accepted for this programme. The materials that matter are: (1) the MANDATORY structured Excel 'study career' file, downloaded from the application portal together with a PDF example of a correctly filled-in file — BOTH worksheets must be completed (tab 'Admission title' and tab 'Other university courses') and the file must be uploaded in the portal as an Excel file, not converted to PDF; (2) for applicants who graduated in Italy, self-declaration of the exams passed — failure to do so means exclusion; (3) for applicants who graduated abroad, upload of the academic transcript — failure to do so means exclusion; (4) an OPTIONAL Curriculum Vitae, uploaded as a PDF in the portal under 'Curriculum vitae', scored up to 4 points. No file-size, page-count or character limits are published for the CV or the Excel file. Note the asymmetry: the Excel file and the transcript/self-declaration are exclusion-bearing, whereas the CV is optional but forfeits up to 4 ranking points if omitted — for a borderline candidate the CV is effectively compulsory.
interview: Yes, but CONDITIONALLY — the interview is not part of the standard route. It applies only to candidates whose average mark is below 24/30 AND who then fail to achieve a satisfactory result in the curriculum vitae evaluation of their work experience in Software Engineering, Computer Engineering and Applied Computer Science. Such candidates 'are required to undertake an online interview in English', in which 'applicants will be expected to demonstrate their knowledge of topics such as programming concepts and software engineering'. Published dates for 2026/27: Early Bird Application 21 - 22/05/2026; Late Application 28 - 29/07/2026; Additional Application Session 17/09/2026. Candidates concerned receive an e-mail invitation after the application deadline, and the admission document explicitly warns 'Please keep an eye on your email after the application deadline'. Practical implication: an applicant with, say, a 22/30 average and strong professional software experience has a genuine two-stage path in rather than an automatic rejection.
conditional_admission: Two distinct conditional regimes. (1) NOT YET GRADUATED AT APPLICATION: 'You can apply if you have acquired at least 120 credit points (ECTS). In this case you will be admitted conditionally.' The diploma must be submitted by the enrolment deadline — 13 October 2026, 12 midday. In the published ranking lists these candidates are flagged with an asterisk: 5 of the 9 admitted EU applicants in the Early Bird session (ranks 1, 3, 5, 6, 7) and 4 of the 30 admitted non-EU applicants carried the asterisk, so provisional admission is common rather than exceptional. Note the 120-ECTS threshold is the standard master-level figure here — the higher 140-ECTS variant applies to Data Analytics, not to this programme. (2) IF YOU GRADUATE AFTER THE ENROLMENT DEADLINE: 'you cannot enrol and you will lose your place, which will be offered to the subsequent applicant in the ranking list.' unibz gives explicit tactical advice not to pay the tuition fees to secure admission in that situation; instead a late enrolment request may be submitted to the Rector and, ONLY if places remain, enrolment is possible by 11 December 2026. Separately, applicants with qualifications gained abroad who have not uploaded their diploma are provisionally admitted until their title can be verified, and ALL non-EU citizens living abroad are provisionally admitted pending official communication from the Italian consulate directly to unibz. Finally, an applicant found not to possess a valid admission qualification can be excluded by Rector's decree even after enrolment.
ofa_rules: NOT APPLICABLE — no OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning obligations) regime exists for this programme. The admission document contains no OFA section, and the published ranking lists contain no OFA markings (the asterisks in these lists denote provisional admission pending completion of the bachelor degree, not OFA). OFA at unibz is a bachelor-level instrument used where a compulsory mathematics test is failed (Economics and Management, Economics Politics and Ethics, Tourism Sport and Event Management) or where mathematics school grades score 3/5 or less (Bachelor in Computer Science). At master level the equivalent function is served instead by the curricular ECTS prerequisites, which must be satisfied BEFORE admission rather than remedied afterwards. The Mathematics pre-course held 21/09 - 09/10/2026 is an optional preparatory offering for incoming students, not an OFA obligation.
language_requirements: Minimal and single-language: English at B2 (CEFR) to gain admission, and nothing else. The admission document states 'The official teaching language is English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure: Entry level (to gain admission) English: B2.' The requirement is ELIMINATORY — failing it means exclusion from the admission procedure, not a lower rank — but it carries no points in the ranking. No Italian, no German, and no third language is required at any stage: not for admission, not to sit examinations, and not to graduate. Proof is uploaded in the application portal under 'upload language certificates' and/or 'enrol for language exams' after creating an application. A final certificate awarded by an Italian public institution requires a self-declaration; one awarded by a foreign public institution requires an uploaded scanned copy of the original. Free Language Centre courses in German and Italian remain available to enrolled students as an optional benefit. Empirical severity check: in the 2026/27 Late session exactly one applicant was excluded for not meeting the language requirement, and the Early Bird lists record no language-based exclusion block at all — a striking contrast with unibz's trilingual programmes.
entry_levels_by_position: Single-language pattern — 1st language English B2; no 2nd language; no 3rd language. Expressed in the schema's positional notation this is 'B2 / none / none', the simplest profile at unibz and materially easier than the B2/B2/none of the trilingual Bachelor in Computer Science or the C1/B2/none of Public Policy and Accounting and Finance. Because there is only one teaching language, the usual unibz logic of ranking languages by the candidate's own strength does not apply here: the requirement attaches to English specifically. Only B2-level exams can be registered for at the unibz Language Centre; higher levels (C1) come into play only through the recognition routes, where a high-school or university education delivered in English is recognised as C1.
exit_levels: NONE — there is no language requirement to graduate from this programme. The admission document's 'Language requirements' section lists only 'Entry level (to gain admission)' and, unlike the trilingual programmes' documents, contains no 'Exit level (to graduate)' subsection at all. This is corroborated by the unibz study guide, which records language obligations only for the older cohorts of this degree: students enrolled in 2021/22 had to attend A1.1 German and Italian courses, and the 2022/23 cohort had to prove A1 CEFR in German and/or Italian or attend Language Centre courses, while from 2023/24 onward no language proficiency requirement is attached. The current study plan likewise contains no language course among its 120 ECTS. Consequently a student admitted with English B2 can complete the degree without ever raising a language level — a substantial practical difference from unibz's trilingual degrees, where graduation demands C1/C1/B2 and is a real gate.
third_language_exam_threshold: NOT APPLICABLE. The B1-in-the-third-language rule for sitting curricular examinations exists only in unibz's trilingual programmes, where courses are delivered in German, Italian and English. This programme is taught entirely in English, so there is no second or third language in which examinations are held and therefore no threshold to meet. Correspondingly, the mid-January English-B1 deadline that applies to trilingual students whose third language is English is irrelevant here, since English is the sole and required language at B2 from the outset.
proof_pathways: Four recognised pathways, all specific to English: (1) THE MAIN TEACHING LANGUAGE OF THE FINAL HIGH SCHOOL YEAR, if English — recognised as C1; for foreign qualifications, if the medium of instruction is not clearly stated on the diploma, a letter or document issued by the high school stating it must also be uploaded. (2) A BACHELOR OR MASTER DEGREE TAUGHT IN ENGLISH — recognised as C1; unibz graduates upload the certificates obtained and/or declare Language Centre exams passed (B2, B2+ or C1); for foreign degrees, if the teaching language is not clearly stated on the degree, a letter or document from the university stating the medium of instruction during the studies must be uploaded. This route is particularly relevant to this programme, since many applicants hold an English-taught computing bachelor. (3) A RECOGNISED LANGUAGE CERTIFICATE from the official unibz list; if it cannot be uploaded it may be sent by e-mail as a PDF or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline. (4) LANGUAGE EXAMS ORGANISED BY THE UNIBZ LANGUAGE CENTRE, registered online through the application portal under 'enrol for language exams' after filling out an application — Early Bird: 16/03/2026 (registration 02 - 09/03/2026) and 16 - 17 and 20 - 21/04/2026 (registration 24/03 - 08/04/2026); Late: 22 - 26/06/2026 (registration 28/05 - 15/06/2026). If an application is started outside a registration period, the applicant must return to the portal during one of those periods to register. CRITICAL SESSION-SPECIFIC GAP: no unibz language exam is offered for the Additional Application Session (18/08 - 04/09/2026), so applicants in that window must already hold an external certificate such as LanguageCert, TOEFL or IELTS.
certificate_rules: Governed by Resolution of the University Council no. 16/2026 ('Recognised language certificates and diplomas — Students and applicants'). To be recognised, a certificate must (1) include the assessment in all FOUR SKILLS and be issued by the certification organisation itself, and (2) indicate adequate performance in all skills in the form of an overall grade, or the detailed assessment must appear on the certificate itself or in appropriate documentation faithful to the original from the certification organisation. Further rules, quoted from the resolution: 'If no overall result and/or level is stated on the certificate, the lowest level reached in one of the subskills is decisive for determining the level, provided that this part of the examination has been passed.' 'There is no compensation for "failed" parts of the exam and no averages are calculated unless these provided by the certification organisation.' 'Certificates issued by exam boards and obtained by taking an online exam ("home edition") are not recognised, except for those explicitly indicated in the list.' 'Certificates regarding single skills issued by different certification organisations will not be accepted.' 'Certificates of participation, certificates of end-of-course-tests and examinations from private educational institutions as well as results of placement tests will not be recognised.' 'Certificates issued by individual lecturers or teaching staff will not be recognised.' 'DAAD certificates are not recognised.' VALIDITY: 'International language certificates must not be older than five years before the date of their submission. The entire calendar year shall apply from 1 January.' Items listed under 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' have unlimited validity. Practical warning for this programme: because the lowest sub-skill determines the level, an IELTS or TOEFL result with one weak band can drop the applicant below B2 and trigger exclusion even when the overall score looks comfortable. Full list: https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf
application_deadline_eu: Three sessions for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment (unibz publishes DD/MM/YYYY; ISO normalised below). EARLY BIRD APPLICATION: 02/03 - 28/04/2026 by noon local time = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. LATE APPLICATION (EU only): 28/05 - 08/07/2026 by noon local time = 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-08. ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION (EU only, opened by the Faculty in August/September if places remain): 18/08 - 04/09/2026 by noon local time = 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04. The Master in Software Engineering IS listed as open for this Additional Session for 2026/27, which is consistent with the EU quota being far from filled (9 + 3 = 12 admitted against 30 EU places). EU applicants may apply for more than one study programme, and an applicant excluded in the first session may apply again in the second. All deadlines are 'by noon local time' — a 12:00 CET cut-off, not end of day.
application_deadline_non_eu: ONE window only for non-EU citizens living outside Italy: the EARLY BIRD APPLICATION, 02/03 - 28/04/2026 by noon local time = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. The admission document states: 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' Non-EU applicants living abroad are NOT eligible for the Late Application or the Additional Application Session, pay a non-refundable €50 application fee, are ranked on a separate list against a separate 30-place quota, and must additionally pre-enrol on the Universitaly portal (one programme only) to obtain the study visa. For this programme the single non-EU window is the binding constraint that matters most: it closed on 2026-04-28 and, as of the verification date (2026-08-29), no further non-EU intake for 2026/27 exists.
parity_of_treatment: Two categories are treated as EU applicants — the critical third category for Turkish and other non-EU applicants already in Italy. (1) Citizens of Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State. (2) Non-EU citizens with a valid Italian permit to stay ('permesso di soggiorno') under article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25/07/1998 — for WORK, FAMILY reasons, POLITICAL or HUMANITARIAN ASYLUM, or RELIGIOUS reasons. Such applicants apply directly to the University and must submit a copy of the valid permit; if it has expired, a renewal request must be attached. 'A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not valid.' CRITICAL WARNING: 'if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin.' For THIS programme the stakes of that classification are unusually high and run in the applicant's favour: parity status moves a candidate from the fiercely contested non-EU list (30 places, waiting list to rank 65) to the undersubscribed EU list (30 places, only 12 admitted across both sessions), and additionally unlocks the Late and Additional sessions and removes the €50 fee. The non-EU ranking list also notes that applicants holding a qualifying permit are ranked together with the relevant group per article 39 paragraph 5.
places_quotas: Three separate quota figures for 2026/27. EU CITIZENS AND CITIZENS GIVEN PARITY OF TREATMENT: Early Bird Application 20 places, Late Application 10 places — 30 EU in total. NON-EU CITIZENS LIVING ABROAD: Early Bird Application 30 places, and no non-EU quota in any later session. The brochure summarises this as 'Places available: 30 EU + 30 non-EU', i.e. 60 places overall. Carry-over rule: for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only, any places remaining unfilled after the Early Bird session are offered in the Late Application. ACTUAL 2026/27 UPTAKE reveals a dramatic split. EU: only 9 admitted in the Early Bird session against 20 places, and only 3 admitted in the Late session — 12 of 30 EU places taken, which is why the Additional Session was opened. NON-EU: all 30 places filled, plus a WAITING LIST running from rank 31 to rank 65 (35 further ranked candidates), with waiting-list candidates contacted by e-mail from 8 June 2026 if places open up; applicants beyond rank 65 were excluded outright for not meeting the admission requirements. Bottom line: an EU or parity-status applicant meeting the prerequisites is very likely to be admitted, while a non-EU applicant abroad faces at least 2.2 ranked competitors per place.
ranking_and_enrolment_dates: EARLY BIRD: ranking lists published by 27/05/2026 (the signed list is dated Bozen-Bolzano, 21.05.2026); payment of the 1st instalment of tuition fees (€600 — this is what secures the place) by 05/06/2026 noon; enrolment from 10/07 to 13/10/2026 noon; non-EU waiting-list candidates contacted from 8 June 2026. LATE APPLICATION: ranking lists by 30/07/2026 (signed list dated 23/07/2026); 1st instalment by 06/08/2026 noon; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 13/10/2026 noon. ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION: ranking lists by 18/09/2026; 1st instalment by 25/09/2026 noon; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 13/10/2026 noon. Note that unlike the bachelor programmes, whose enrolment windows close in August or September, ALL THREE sessions here share the same late enrolment deadline of 13/10/2026. Missing either the payment or the enrolment deadline means automatic exclusion and the place passes to the next applicant on the list. An applicant admitted to more than one programme may secure up to 2 places by paying the instalment twice, and by confirming a place renounces admission to the others. Paying the fee does NOT confer student status — only enrolment does — and there is no refund if you pay but do not enrol, except for non-EU applicants abroad who fail to obtain the necessary documents from the Italian authorities in their country. A residual late-enrolment route exists until 11 December 2026 for candidates who graduate after the enrolment deadline, but only if places remain. Appeals against the ranking decree may be lodged with the Bozen-Bolzano Administrative Court within 60 days of notification or publication.
programme_specific_dates: Dates specific to this programme rather than shared university-wide. ONLINE INTERVIEWS (only for candidates below the 24/30 average whose CV evaluation was unsatisfactory): Early Bird 21 - 22/05/2026; Late 28 - 29/07/2026; Additional Application Session 17/09/2026. SIGNED RANKING-LIST DATES: Early Bird 21.05.2026, Late 23/07/2026 — note the Early Bird list is signed the same week as the interviews, so the interview-to-ranking turnaround is only days. NON-EU WAITING-LIST ACTIVATION: from 8 June 2026. LANGUAGE EXAM SESSIONS: 16/03/2026 (registration 02 - 09/03/2026); 16 - 17 and 20 - 21/04/2026 (registration 24/03 - 08/04/2026); 22 - 26/06/2026 (registration 28/05 - 15/06/2026) — with none offered in the Additional Session. LATE ENROLMENT BACKSTOP: 11 December 2026. Start-of-year dates for 2026/27: intensive language courses 01 - 18/09/2026 (Mon-Fri, 6 h/day, not available to Additional Session applicants); Mathematics pre-course 21/09 - 09/10/2026; Freshers Days 28 - 29/09/2026. Academic calendar: 1st semester classes 28/09 - 23/12/2026, holidays 24/12/2026 - 06/01/2027, classes 07 - 23/01/2027, exams 25/01 - 20/02/2027; 2nd semester classes 01/03 - 25/03/2027, holidays 26 - 29/03/2027, classes 30/03 - 12/06/2027, exams 14/06 - 10/07/2027; autumn exam session 23/08 - 25/09/2027. There are no portfolio-submission or written-exam dates because neither instrument is used.
required_documents: AT APPLICATION (online via the Application Portal, https://aws.unibz.it/exup/): a valid ID card or passport, front and back — 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'; the completed online form; the MANDATORY structured Excel 'study career' file downloaded from the portal (along with a PDF example of a filled-in file), with BOTH worksheets completed — tab 'Admission title' and tab 'Other university courses' — and uploaded as an Excel file; for applicants who graduated in Italy, self-declaration of the exams passed, otherwise exclusion; for applicants who graduated abroad, upload of the academic transcript, otherwise exclusion; an optional Curriculum Vitae as a PDF under 'Curriculum vitae' (worth up to 4 points); English language proof under 'upload language certificates' and/or registration under 'enrol for language exams'; the diploma of the qualification if already obtained abroad (if not yet held, it is uploaded at enrolment); for non-EU citizens resident in Italy claiming parity of treatment, a copy of the valid permit to stay plus a renewal request if expired. Once submitted, the application CANNOT be modified, and forms filled in but not correctly sent are disregarded. 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list.' The Admission Committee evaluates ONLY documents uploaded by the application deadline. AT ENROLMENT, holders of a foreign university degree must upload: the bachelor degree diploma; an official translation of the degree into Italian (not necessary if issued in German or English); and the Diploma Supplement, which must indicate that at least 180 ECTS were achieved and that the qualification gives access to a master programme — plus the ARDI and/or CIMEA statements described under credential_recognition. Students transferring from another Italian university must submit a copy of the transfer application to the Student Office at the start of the academic year. Non-EU students must hand in a copy of the residence permit to the Student Office once obtained.
application_fee: €50, payable ONLY by non-EU citizens living outside Italy. The admission document states plainly: 'Application fee: € 50.' It is an administration fee and is non-refundable. EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment — including non-EU nationals holding a qualifying Italian permit to stay for work, family, asylum or religious reasons — pay no application fee. Because non-EU applicants abroad have only a single application window, the fee is a one-off rather than a per-session cost.
tuition_or_fees_link: Total tuition fees are €1,200 per year, in two instalments: 1st instalment €600, which includes the €16 revenue stamp (marca da bollo) and is the payment that secures the place after admission; 2nd instalment €600, to be paid by March of the following year. Over the two-year programme that is roughly €2,400. Delayed payment of the second instalment incurs a fine; unpaid fees block exam-taking and any transfer to another university or study programme. No refund if you drop out, interrupt your studies or are excluded. Exemptions: students with a disability recognised under article 3, paragraph 1 of Law no. 104/1992 or with a disability of 66% or more (health-authority certificate to be handed in at the start of the academic year), and foreign students granted a scholarship from the Italian government. Students awarded a scholarship by the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to a refund of the tuition fees. Fees detail is published inside the admission-information PDF (https://www.unibz.it/assets/CoursesPDF/master-in-software-engineering_admission-information_en_GB.pdf) and on the general fees page https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees/
scholarships_grants: The main route is the income-based provincial study grant from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano, administered by the Office for Higher Education Support / Office for the Right to Study and applied for online through the provincial e-government service, with form-filling assistance from the South Tyrolean Students Association (ASUS). Three instruments exist: ordinary study grants, merit scholarships, and grants for fostering postgraduate studies. Grant holders also receive reimbursement of the tuition fees paid for the academic year. CRITICAL RESTRICTION FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS: 'Non-EU students can apply for a study grant only if they have a long-time residence permit or after they have had their residence in South Tyrol for at least one year without interruption' — so a newly arrived non-EU first-year student is effectively ineligible in year one, and on a two-year master that means the grant is realistically available only for the second year. unibz itself grants tuition-fee exemptions rather than cash scholarships (disability, Italian government scholarship holders). No programme-specific scholarship is published for the Master in Software Engineering. Contact: study@unibz.it, +39 0471 012900. Reference page: https://guide.unibz.it/en/life-on-campus/study-grants
credential_recognition: At enrolment, holders of a foreign university degree must upload the bachelor degree diploma, an official translation into Italian (not necessary if the documents were issued in German or English), and the Diploma Supplement indicating that at least 180 ECTS were achieved and that the qualification gives access to a master programme. Then, depending on the education system: (a) EU COUNTRIES, SWITZERLAND, NORWAY, ICELAND, LIECHTENSTEIN — a Statement of Correspondence of the bachelor degree, downloaded from ARDI (Automatic Recognition Database Italy, https://ardi.cimea.it/en); (b) NON-EU COUNTRIES THAT ARE SIGNATORIES TO THE LISBON CONVENTION — a Statement of Correspondence from ARDI AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA; (c) NON-EU COUNTRIES NOT SIGNATORIES OF THE LISBON CONVENTION — a Statement of Comparability issued by CIMEA AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA. Türkiye is a signatory of the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so Turkish applicants normally fall under case (b): ARDI Statement of Correspondence + CIMEA Statement of Verification. unibz performs its own checks and 'in case of doubt reserves the right to request additional documents'; applicants with a foreign title are provisionally admitted until the title can be verified, and 'if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment'. Distinct from title recognition, the CURRICULAR requirements for foreign qualifications are verified on content: 'For candidates with a qualification obtained abroad the verification of the curricular requirements is based on the specific contents of the educational activities' — which is why the Excel study-career file and the academic transcript are exclusion-bearing documents. Recognition of credit points from previous university studies is possible only after enrolment and only where the exams taken elsewhere are equivalent in content to unibz courses. Signatory list: https://www.enic-naric.net/ ; CIMEA services: https://cimea-diplome.it/
non_eu_visa_process: Sequence for non-EU citizens living abroad: apply to unibz in the Early Bird window only (€50 non-refundable fee) → appear on the separate non-EU ranking list (30 places, waiting list to rank 65) → if admitted, secure the place by paying the €600 first instalment by 05/06/2026 noon → THEN start the visa application by pre-enrolling on the Universitaly portal of the Ministry of University and Research. The Universitaly application is MANDATORY, 'otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol', and only ONE study programme may be selected there. The Italian diplomatic-consular authorities in the applicant's country then issue the entry visa for studies/university. unibz publishes three explicit caveats: 'the application at unibz does not guarantee an appointment at the diplomatic-consular Italian representation'; 'the admission to unibz does not confer automatically any right to obtaining a visa'; and 'obtaining a study visa issued by the competent diplomatic-consular representation does not automatically confer any right to enrolment'. Additionally, all non-EU citizens living abroad are only provisionally admitted, the requirement being the official communication sent by the Italian consulate abroad directly to unibz. FINANCIAL MEANS: at least €800 per month for living costs (accommodation, food, study materials, leisure), excluding tuition fees, with a total of approximately €24,000 to be demonstrated for a two-year master programme (inclusive of the ca. €1,200/year tuition); health insurance and visa expenses are budgeted separately. AFTER ARRIVAL: the residence permit ('permesso di soggiorno') must be applied for 'within 8 working days since your arrival in Italy' — contact the Advisory Service immediately on arrival — and once obtained a copy must be handed in to the Student Office in person or by e-mail. WORK: no more than 20 hours a week and no more than 1,040 hours per year. REFUND EXCEPTION: non-EU applicants abroad who pay the instalment but do not obtain the documents necessary for enrolment from the Italian authorities in their country are entitled to a refund. Universitaly: https://www.universitaly.it/

uncertainty_notes: Data year: all figures are for academic year 2026/27; the admission-information PDF carries 'Latest update: 25.08.2026' and the express caveat 'Subject to change.' Verified 2026-08-29. TIMING STATUS AT VERIFICATION: the Early Bird and Late sessions have CLOSED and their ranking lists are published; only the Additional Application Session (18/08 - 04/09/2026, EU citizens only) is still open, and the Master in Software Engineering is listed as accepting applications in it. The non-EU window for 2026/27 closed on 2026-04-28 and cannot be reopened. (1) SCORING GAP IN THE OFFICIAL TEXT: the curricular-ECTS scale reads '1 point for 41-80 ECTS' and '0 points for less than 40 ECTS', leaving exactly 40 ECTS unassigned. This is an error or ambiguity in the source document, not in this record; a candidate with exactly 40 ECTS should ask the Faculty. (2) SSD CODE INCONSISTENCY WITHIN THE SAME DOCUMENT: the entry-requirements section uses the post-2024-reform codes (INFO-01/A, IINF-05/A, MATH-01/A, MATH-03/A, MATH-05/A) with legacy equivalents in brackets, while the admission-procedure scoring section uses only the OLD codes (INF/01, ING-INF/05, MAT/01, MAT/05, MAT/08). They refer to the same sectors; the discrepancy is editorial. (3) STALE DATE IN THE RANKING LISTS: both the Early Bird and Late ranking-list PDFs contain a paragraph stating late enrolment 'by 12 December 2025' while every other passage in the same documents, and the admission-information PDF, says 11 December 2026. The 2025 date is a copy-paste leftover from the previous academic year; 11 December 2026 is the operative deadline. (4) PLACES PRESENTATION: the brochure's '30 EU + 30 non-EU' and the admission PDF's split of the EU quota into 20 Early Bird + 10 Late reconcile (20+10=30); the PDF split is authoritative for per-session planning. (5) EXIT LANGUAGE LEVEL: the finding that there is NO graduation language requirement rests on two mutually supporting sources — the admission PDF's Language requirements section lists only an entry level, in structural contrast to the trilingual programmes' PDFs which carry an explicit 'Exit level (to graduate)' subsection, and the unibz study guide records language obligations only for the 2021/22 and 2022/23 cohorts of this degree and none from 2023/24 onward. It is a well-supported conclusion rather than a directly quoted 'there is no exit requirement' statement. (6) SCHOLARSHIP AMOUNTS are not confirmed for 2026/27 — the €1,680-€6,960 range and any merit-average threshold come from secondary summaries, not from a page verified for this programme; the provincial call sets amounts annually. (7) No separate call/manifesto document was found in English; a Rector's decree may exist only in the Italian albo. (8) ADDITIONAL SESSION QUOTA: the additional-session page confirms the programme is open but does not publish the number of remaining places; the residual EU capacity is inferable as up to 18 (30 EU places minus 12 admitted) but is not officially stated. (9) TURKISH-APPLICANT RELEVANCE: Türkiye is a Lisbon Convention signatory, so case (b) recognition applies (ARDI Statement of Correspondence + CIMEA Statement of Verification); this classification is inferred from the convention's membership, not stated by unibz for this programme. (10) The Webometrics bonus depends on the applicant's home university position in a ranking that is republished twice yearly; unibz does not state which edition/date of the ranking is used, which materially affects candidates near a band boundary. (11) The programme's renaming history (from 'Master in Software Engineering for Information Systems', with students enrolled before 2023/24 on the old programme) means older third-party pages, forum posts and course lists may describe a different curriculum; the brochure itself still publishes a legacy 'enroled form 2024' study plan alongside the current one.
